thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated container restarts and OOMs observed on inference-us-east-1 cluster (nodes: rt-gpu-1, rt-gpu-2). Pattern: slow memory siphon from KV cache / paged-attention allocator leading to gradual resident set growth and eventual process crash. Tagging on-call.

Alex: seeing it too. multiple restarts over last 12m. 95p latency for streaming requests jumped from 120ms -> 800ms.

Maria: any customer-facing symptoms?

Alex: yes — a handful of active customers reported intermittent 5xx and truncated streams. Not widespread yet but trending.

incident-bot: metric summary (last 30m):
```
oom_kills: 6
container_restarts: 9
avg_rss_gb: 12.3 -> 18.6
pager_evictions/sec: 0.3 -> 0.02
error_rate(ingress): 0.9% -> 6.7%
```

Raj: logs show allocator returning ENOMEM on reserve path before kernel OOM. attached snippet: 
```
[2026-03-15T01:02:12Z] runtime: failed to allocate 524288 bytes: allocator: paged-attn: slot_alloc() -> ENOMEM
[2026-03-15T01:02:12Z] cuda: cuMemAlloc returned CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY on gpu0
[2026-03-15T01:02:13Z] container: exit code 137
```

Jen: looks like fragments accumulate in the KV bitmap, then a double-free-ish reclaim fails under pressure. Could be race in async page compaction.

Tom: is there a cheap mitigation we can do live to stop customer impact?

Alex: immediate ideas: 1) reduce max sequence length and force smaller KV cache growth, 2) throttle low-priority traffic, 3) fallback to non-paged attention model variant per routing policy.

Maria: I'm starting throttles on the affected routes now. Running: `curl -XPOST https://internal-router/route/throttle -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","p":0.3}'` - will report.

Raj: I can deploy a targeted routing rule to divert traffic from rt-gpu-1/2 to rt-gpu-hotpool that uses non-paged model variant (higher cost but stable). Doing canary of 10% -> 50% if healthy.

incident-bot: deploy-bot: initiating canary routing change: 10% -> non-paged-variant for tenants with active streams.

Alex: also pushing a config patch to reduce in-memory page window: `REDWOOD_PAGER_WINDOW=8` and `PAGER_EVICT_WATERMARK=0.6` — low-risk config flip, can revert.

Jen: quick check: do we have a hotfix branch with compaction fix? If not, let's avoid code deploy. We should rely on routing and config flips.

Tom: rolling the config now to rt-gpu-2 only. patch applied. watching RSS.

incident-bot: config change acknowledged on rt-gpu-2.

Alex: rt-gpu-2 RSS stabilized to 14.1GB from 18.6GB within 60s. No new OOMs on that node. rt-gpu-1 still creeping.

Maria: increasing throttle to 50% on /v1/generate globally for 5m window to give us breathing room.

Raj: can we safely evict cold KV entries proactively? There's a script: `scripts/pager/evict_cold.sh --age 120` but it needs a rolling permission bump.

Jen: be cautious — forced evict may spike latencies and cause transient misses. But acceptable if it prevents OOM. I'd run on one node first.

Tom: I ran `evict_cold.sh --age 60` on rt-gpu-1 (dry-run) then `--age 120` live. Observed immediate free of ~1.2GB. No crashes yet.

Alex: good. I'm opening a temporary alert suppression for noise while we stabilize.

incident-bot: customer-impact-checklist:
- active customers affected: 3 (short stream truncation)
- SLO breaches: stream latency spikes, transient 5xx for subset
- billing/comms: SEs notified for affected accounts

Maria: pinging SE to inform customers and open support ticket templates.

Raj: scheduled an emergency pull-request to introduce faster compaction path (no blocking IO) — PR link: https://github.com/redwood/serving/pull/8432 (WIP). Will not merge to prod during incident.

Jen: call with eng-ml ops in 15m to review allocator invariant and plan postmortem.

Tom: next steps for live mitigation checklist:
- keep throttles 30-50% until both nodes stabilized
- route 60% traffic away from paged variant to non-paged (rollback if latency > 1.5s)
- run cold-evict on remaining nodes one-by-one
- do not deploy runtime code changes now

Alex: summary for handoff -> Maria will take over in 10m. Key facts: paged-attn allocator leaking/fragmenting, temporary mitigations applied (throttle, routing to non-paged, config window shrink, cold-evict), customers notified.

Maria: taking it. Notes saved to incident doc: https://internal.wiki/incidents/2432109876 (I'll update). leaving channel to follow up with SEs.

incident-bot: escalation: schedule postmortem with eng-runtime + eng-ml + eng-sre. Assigning owners: Raj (root-cause), Jen (mitigation verification), Alex (customer comms).

Maria: handing over to next on-call rotation (see runbook -> Runbook: Paged Attn Memory Creep). If anything spikes, ping me direct. :wave:

Tom: thanks team. I'll monitor logs and keep an eye on any regressions.

Alex: closing thread for now, will re-open if we see fresh OOMs. :thumbsup:
